segments.text: Today we're diving into Pydantic
settings, which is a small but powerful
library that builds on top of Pydantic
and it makes managing application
configuration very easy and also
type-safe in Python. So, this package
builds on top of Pydantic's validation
system and it gives you a clean and
declarative way to handle configuration.
We're going to look at how it can be
used to read in values from environment
variables and also from a .env file and
how we can use type checking to control
the types of inputs that we are going to
accept in our settings. So, let's get
started. Before we do, if you want to
support the channel, check out our
coffee page. We've got a link just below

get started looking at Pydantic
settings. Now, it's worth noting that

Pydantic website. But, it is a separate

open up a project that I have in VS Code
and this is a very simple FastAPI
application that has a single route and
that's this health check route here. And
at the bottom, because I'm using UVI,
we're going to run the UVI add command
and we can install Pydantic settings
using this command here. And this is
[clears throat] the recommended way of
dealing with settings in a FastAPI

system environment. So, an environment
variable is something that lives outside
of the code base in the operating system
and it can be read in by Python and also
by other programs as well. Now, any
environment variable that you do read in
